Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old woman with SLE on methotrexate presenting with 1 day of shortness of breath, pleuritic right-sided back pain, and two episodes of hemoptysis; subjective fever; plan for same-day in-person assessment for suspected chest infection/pneumonia.

History:
- Presenting complaint: New-onset breathlessness and right-sided back pain with deep inspiration since today; coughed up blood twice today; subjective fever.
- Associated symptoms: Feels heart beating more than usual; fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, and difficulty with daily activities for ~2 weeks.
- Pertinent negatives: Denies smoking. No recent long-haul travel. No personal or family history of blood clots. No medication or other allergies reported.
- Past medical history: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
- Medications: Methotrexate (dose/route/frequency not documented); last taken this morning.
- Social history: Works a desk job; lives alone in a flat; has a cat; non-smoker.

Examination:
- Vitals: Heart rate estimated via patient radial pulse count ~66–74 bpm.
- General: Clinician stated patient does not appear acutely unstable on video assessment.
- Capillary refill: Appeared normal on video-guided test.
- Oropharynx: Visualized via phone; no specific abnormalities documented.
- Neck: Patient self-palpation of cervical nodes; no enlargement reported.

Impression:
- Suspected chest infection; assessment needed to rule in/out pneumonia as cause of pleuritic pain and hemoptysis.

Plan:
- Arrange same-day face-to-face clinic review for chest auscultation and measurement of blood pressure, pulse, and temperature.
- No antibiotics prescribed now; may require antibiotic treatment pending in-person assessment findings.
- If symptoms do not settle, may require follow-up chest X-ray.
- Support team number to be used to book the same-day in-person appointment.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - Full set of vitals (BP, temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation).
  - Lung examination findings.
  - Methotrexate dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Comprehensive allergy verification beyond patient report (no list available).
● Internal conflicts:
  - Patient name documented as “Tracy Chapman” earlier and “Doris” later (conflict noted).
  - Patient reports feeling heart racing, but pulse count on call ~66–74 bpm (conflict noted).
● Transcript quality:
  - Minor inaudible/elliptical segments; overall sufficient to capture key clinical details.
